thesis: Equivalence is relative to aligned observations, policies, horizons and finite testing resources.

ideas.statement: A common contract supports trajectory-distance comparisons while finite observers restrict which differences can be detected.
Failed finite tests do not certify equivalence: the observed separating maximum is a lower bound on possible distinguishability.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Short-seed output can be statistically far from uniform yet computationally hard to distinguish.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Distances classify representational adequacy rather than degrees of reality; interface alignment cannot be changed opportunistically.

audit.notes: Complete batch read; headings and navigation excluded from idea ranking.
